name: Z.ai GLM Coding Plan
notes: Subscription with 5-hour and weekly credit limits and no per-token prices; each model carries the Z.ai API list prices of the same model, so Cost is what a request would cost there. Takes a GLM Coding Plan API key, which since 2026-10-16 is separate from a standard Z.ai API key and not interchangeable with it. The Coding Plan docs name only GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash; requests for GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.1 are routed to GLM-5.3 and requests for GLM-4.7 to GLM-5.3-Flash, so only the two are shipped. Global region only. Caching is automatic. Reasoning: thinking cannot be disabled on GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, and the docs list only low, high and max as their reasoning_effort values; no quirk maps the gateway's efforts onto them, and this is untested live. Quota exhaustion: Z.ai answers HTTP 429 with {"error":{"code":"1308",...}}, the code sent as a string, so exhaustedErrorCodes lists the usage-limit codes 1308, 1309, 1310 and 1316 to 1321 as strings; the rate-limit codes 1302 and 1313 and code 1311 are left out and stay a Cooldown. No quota endpoint is documented, so there is no quota reader. Not flagged for Terms Risk (ADR 0099): Z.ai publishes the Coding Plan endpoint and how to call it, though the Subscription Terms (section 4) limit the quota to officially supported tools, name SDK-based access and other third-party integrations as unauthorized, and forbid to "resell, sub-resell, repackage, aggregate, proxy" or otherwise provide the plan to any third party. The plan is licensed to one person, so sharing the gateway with other people breaches it.
